7.3 — Ladders I: The Climbing State

Walk. Jump. Climb. Your player is about to grow a third movement mode — one that turns gravity OFF, reads a new input axis, and exists only because a trigger said so. Ladders are your second full state machine, and you already know every pattern it needs.

Predict First ~10 min

The design, before any code — four states of the body:

StateGravityControlsAnimation
Top-down (overworld)0WASD translateWalkDir
Grounded (platformer)2A/D translate, Space jumpIsWalking + jump
Climbing (new)0W/S translateclimb/idle-on-ladder
Airborne2(no control — physics)jump/fall

Predict: climbing turns gravityScale to 0 — the same number the overworld uses in Start (5.3). Why does the SAME zero mean two different things there and here? And why must vertical input SLOW the climb (speed 3, not 5)? When do you want a ladder to feel deliberate?

Socratic

The ladder changes state via a TRIGGER enter/exit pair — OnTriggerEnter2D sets isOnLadder, OnTriggerExit2D clears it. Compare that with the lever's remembered toggle (5.2): why is a zone remembered only while you are IN it, but a lever remembered forever? What does each design assume about the player's intent?

Build Lab ~25 min

Step 1 — the zone. Build a ladder: a tall trigger collider (Is Trigger checked!) tagged "Ladder" (make the tag — 2.3 ritual) plus whatever ladder art you have in the starter sprites. The collider IS the ladder; the art is a costume.

Step 2 — the state fields. In PlayerController, same voice as always:

[SerializeField] private float climbSpeed = 3f;
private bool isOnLadder = false;

private void OnTriggerEnter2D(Collider2D other)
{
    if (other.CompareTag("Ladder")) isOnLadder = true;
}

private void OnTriggerExit2D(Collider2D other)
{
    if (other.CompareTag("Ladder")) isOnLadder = false;
}

Step 3 — the climb movement. In Update, INSIDE the isPlatformer branch (ladders are cave-only!), add a climbing lane:

if (isOnLadder)
{
    rb.gravityScale = 0;                 // the ladder owns gravity
    float vDirection = Input.GetAxis("Vertical");
    Vector2 vVector = new Vector2(0, vDirection * climbSpeed * Time.deltaTime);
    transform.Translate(vVector);

    if (Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.Space)) // jump OFF the ladder
    {
        isOnLadder = false;  // ...but the exit trigger will not fire!
        rb.gravityScale = 2;
        rb.AddForce(Vector2.up * jumpForce, ForceMode2D.Impulse);
    }
}
else
{
    rb.gravityScale = 2;                // normal platformer gravity
    // ... your existing move/jump code runs here
}

Press Play and climb. You are reading the SAME Vertical axis the overworld uses — one input, three meanings, chosen by state. That is your whole movement course in one if.

Step 4 — the exit bug you must meet. Read the comment in the jump-off code. When you Space off the ladder, you set isOnLadder = false by hand — but if you jumped off but your BODY is still touching the trigger, the NEXT OnTriggerEnter2D does not fire (you never exited!), and… you land and cannot re-climb without stepping out and back in. Fix: keep a one-frame grace or check the trigger each frame. Bugs like this are why trigger state pairs deserve a test ritual.

Bug Hunt: The sticky ladder

  1. Forget the else that restores gravityScale to 2. What happens to the FIRST jump after climbing — and why does the symptom appear far from the cause?
  2. Set climbSpeed to your xSpeed (5). Climb a ladder next to a wall. Why does "responsive" read as "twitchy" — and what did the slower number buy?
  3. Leave gravity at 2 while climbing. What happens at the exact moment you stop pressing W — and why is "sliding down ladders" a REAL GAME FEATURE you just discovered by accident?
  4. Your ladder trigger is 1 tile wide; your player is 1.2 tiles. Describe the exit/enter flicker at the seam — which two Unity messages are firing per frame?
Tinker ~10 min

Tinker: Climb design

  1. Snap: when you enter a ladder's zone horizontally, your x should LOCK to the ladder's x. What would read that value — other.transform.position.x — and where would you store it?
  2. Design a ladder that is a RISK: spikes at the top on one side. What does climbing toward danger do to input speed's meaning?
  3. Hard: climb with an ANIMATION variant (the starter animator may have climb frames — check). Which parameter do you add — and which branch sets it?

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Build a trigger-based ladder zone with its own tag
  • Explain climb as a state: gravity 0, vertical input, else restores
  • Demonstrate and fix the jump-off re-entry bug
  • Explain one input axis serving three meanings via state
